speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Our air, sea and land transport sectors have weathered the worst of the pandemic and emerged stronger, due to the close cooperation between the Government, workers, unions, and industry partners.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: In the next phase, the Ministry of Transport (MOT) will focus on gearing up for growth.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: We will enhance the competitiveness of our global aviation and maritime hubs by strengthening capabilities and sustainability efforts, and creating opportunities for our enterprises and people.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: We will build a sustainable, resilient and inclusive land transport system as part of a liveable city for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: As our anticipated activities return, the Government will work with aviation stakeholders to build up Changi Airport’s operational capacity ahead of demand, and readiness to deal with new threats.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Singapore’s maritime hub stayed resilient and performed well through the pandemic, maintaining our position as the world’s busiest transhipment hub.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: We must build on our strengths to respond adroitly to changes in the global economic landscape and disruptions to supply chains.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: MOT is working with the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore and Changi Airport Group to update the design of T5 to be pandemic-resilient, with greater modularity for flexibility in scaling operations.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The new terminal will also be designed for sustainability with energy-efficient features.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Beyond upgrading our infrastructure, MOT will strengthen capabilities in the aviation and maritime sectors through digitalisation and other innovations.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: To build up our aviation and maritime workforce, we are collaborating with industry partners to reach out to more students, develop work-study programmes, and support job conversions and skills upgrading for mid-career workers.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: We will also invest in our people by redesigning jobs and deepening skillsets.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Sustainability is central to the next phase of growth for our aviation and maritime hubs.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Both sectors will contribute towards the national target to achieve net-zero carbon emissions by 2050.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: We will also require all new harbour craft operating in our port waters to be fully electric, capable of using B100 biofuels or compatible with net-zero fuels such as hydrogen from 2030.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: MOT will also work with the aviation and maritime ecosystems to put the regulatory frameworks, pilots, incentives, and infrastructure in place to facilitate a smooth transition.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: On the global stage, MOT actively supports the efforts of the International Civil Aviation Organization and the International Maritime Organization to reduce emissions from international transport.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: We also work with partners to develop sustainable international aviation and maritime ecosystems, such as "green lanes" for flights powered by sustainable aviation fuels as well as green and digital shipping corridors.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Public transport remains at the heart of our land transport system.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Many participants in our Forward Singapore engagements recognised and appreciated the improvements to our public transport system over the last decade, which have made it more accessible, reliable, and inclusive.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The Government will significantly expand our land transport network over the next decade.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: We are on course to expand our rail network by a further 100 kilometres; when completed, eight in ten homes will be within a ten-minute walk of an MRT station.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Increasing the density of our rail network will make journeys more convenient for commuters, enhance the resilience of the overall system, and contribute significantly towards our net-zero emissions target by encouraging more people to opt for public transport over private vehicles.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: We must also ensure fiscal sustainability, as we invest in building a high-quality, world-class public transport system.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Financing public transport is a shared responsibility across the Government, operators, and commuters.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: We are heartened that participants in our Forward Singapore engagements acknowledged the need for this, while emphasising the importance of affordable public transport fares, especially for the vulnerable and lower-income groups.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The Public Transport Council is reviewing the fare adjustment formula and mechanism, to achieve equitable cost distribution across all stakeholders.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: MOT will further encourage the adoption of cleaner-energy vehicles through regulation, incentives, and infrastructure.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: We have established clear regulatory milestones: to disallow registration of diesel cars and taxis from 2025, and Internal Combustion Engine cars and taxis from 2030.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: We will review financial incentives to encourage the adoption of electric cars, and monitor related developments in other vehicle segments, such as motorcycles and goods vehicles.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: A central theme that emerged from our Forward Singapore engagements was for our transport system to be more inclusive, especially for seniors and persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Features, such as wider footpaths, more greenery, barrier-free crossings and road markings, will inform road users that they are in a Friendly Streets zone.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Where necessary, we will also implement more direct crossings for pedestrians and reduce waiting times for pedestrians at traffic crossings.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Every town will have cycling paths by 2024; these intra-town paths will aid first and last mile connectivity to the major public transport nodes and key amenities.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: We will drive the next bound of growth across our air, sea and land transport sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Together, we will continue to build a more resilient, sustainable and inclusive transport system for all Singaporeans.
